errata: The former 0-of-3^13 result is not a proof of f32-neighborhood infeasibility. It tested every exact floating C_cross residual against >=0 even though the unchanged baseline B itself has 14 negative residuals, all between -8.89e-16 and 0. The direct P/F shoreline reconstruction finds zero B crossing failures.

The earlier row metadata mapping used crossing_rows_json[:C_cross_rows], but 32 sign_only summary records are not matrix rows. Correct mapping filters those summaries first: 560 records = 32 summaries + 528 CSR rows. CSR-derived 13-node support remains valid; row labels from the old positional map do not.

The exact stored C coefficients contain sub-ULP representational artifacts at baseline-pinned variables: for RC (857,1182), the stored single-variable interval has width +5.60981754089469e-17 m; for RC (857,1184), it has width -2.0002362498791288e-16 m. Independent exact-rational P/F/design crossing constraints give width 0 at B for both nodes. The second stored-C contradiction is not a physical crossing contradiction.

For the candidate, 20 C rows below -1e-12 map to direct geometric crossing drift on five native edges, each duplicated across P/F and two adjacent cells. The direct parameter excess is at most 1.8719795342516847e-7 of a 6 m edge (~1.12 micrometers); this is a real exact-geometry violation under the frozen no-slack rule, but no joint f32-neighborhood feasibility result is established.

The old 9-versus-13 comparison counts single-node one-ULP moves that fix at least one strictly negative C row versus the CSR support union. The nine includes a node that only affects two baseline-level ~1e-15 rows. Restricting to 20 material rows gives six individually helpful nodes over ten support nodes. Neither count proves or disproves a simultaneous correction.
scope: Read-only diagnosis. No solver, terrain edits, tolerance changes, or exhaustive neighborhood enumeration were performed in this correction.
